' Testimony of Rep An n Matlack, introducing
LD 1186, Resolve, Directing the Department of Transportation to Study
the Feasibility of Ferry Service to Monhegan Island
Before the Transportation Committee
Good afternoon, Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and respected colleagues on the
Transportation Committee. My name is Ann Matlack and I represent House District 43, which
includes the communities of Cushing, Thomaston, South Thomaston, St George and part of Owls
Head. I am here today to testify Neither For Nor Against LD 1186, a Resolve, Directing the
Department of Transportation to Study the Feasibility of Ferry Service to Monhegan Island.
I'm a bit perplexed as to why there would need to be a study on whether or not to add a state
ferry service for Monhegan Island. As many of the bills here in Transportation today indicate,
there are already concerns with employee recruitment and retention of existing crew members, with overnight docking at mainland ports and emergency services, establishing a permanent oversight committee to ensure sustainable and equitable ferry operations, and increasing the influence of the ferry advisory board on funding and operations within the Maine State Ferry Service. I believe there are sufficient issues with current operations that should be dealt with before adding to the Ferry Service workload.
In addition, there are already two ferry services making runs to Monhegan Isla11d: one seasonal
service, Hardy Boat Cruises out of Bristol and New Harbor; and one year-round service,
Monhegan Boat Line out of Port Clyde, which is part of St George, though the folks who live
there are reluctant to say this in mixed company.
If this bill is to proceed, I would suggest including a representative from at least one of the existing Monhegan ferry lines. They would be able to provide insight into the current operations of service to Monhegan and the logistics of sailing into Monhegan, which is not an easy port to
navigate.

I would be happy to answer any questions you may have.

Feasibility of Ferry Service to Monhegan Island

Before the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation

Good afternoon, Senator Nangle and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Transportation. My name is Lydia Crafts, and I represent House District 46, which includes
Bristol, Damariscotta, Monhegan Plantation, Newcastle and Nobleboro. Today, I am pleased to
present LD 1186, Resolve, Directing the Department of Transportation to Study the
Feasibility of Ferry Service to Monhegan Island.
I have the distinct honor of representing Monhegan Plantation, a rocky island 10 miles off the coast with a year-round population of 64, as of the 2020 census. Seasonal boats cany hundreds
of summer visitors to the island daily from Boothbay, New Harbor and Port Clyde. In the winter,
islanders find themselves limited to boat runs two or three days per week based on the postal contracts. Bad weather can mean trips to shore for medical appointments, which can keep residents on the mainland for five days at a time. This carries a high cost and interferes
significantly with work and family responsibilities.

As Monhegan looks ahead at infrastructure upgrades and wharf improvements, the timing seems appropriate to consider how the Maine State Feny Service (MSFS) might consider possible
service to the island. This will, understandably, be individualized to the specific needs of the
island and the available services of the MSFS. The goal of this resolve is to assess the economic
and social benefits as well as the challenges of implementing ferry service. Additionally it will consider the infrastructure resources and needs of the island and mainland, and the overall financial and operational feasibility of such a service.
I appreciate the committee's consideration of directing the DOT to study this. After additional
communication with current transportation providers, I suggest we add a representative to the proposed study group. I would be happy to work with Ms. Furman to provide an amendment for
the work session.

Thank you for your time. I would be happy to answer any questions.
